title: Latency-Aware Fidelity Gateway — Product Brief and Packaging
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This brief describes the Latency-Aware Fidelity Gateway (LAFG), a product-level capability that dynamically negotiates inference fidelity (model variant, precision, KV cache reuse, and response length) to meet per-route or per-request latency SLOs while optimizing cost and customer-perceived quality. LAFG is intended to be surfaced as a product feature in Redwood Console and via the Redwood API as an opt-in routing and fidelity negotiation layer.

Key problem we solve:
- Customers must choose between maintaining strict latency SLOs or using higher-fidelity, higher-cost model variants.
- Manual variant selection and static capacity reservations lead to excess cost or SLA violations during traffic spikes.
- Developers need a simple contract to express latency versus quality priorities per route.

Primary personas:
- Platform engineers at mid-market and enterprise customers who set per-route SLAs and want predictable latency for user-facing features.
- Product/ML engineers at startups who want low-latency defaults without deep runtime tuning.
- Redwood sales and solutions engineers who sell Dedicated/Private packages with SLA add-ons.

Goals (90-day and 12-month):
1) 90-day:
   - Deliver a gating service that can route requests between two fidelity tiers (high-fidelity and fast-fallback) with transparent telemetry.
   - Expose per-route policy controls in Console for latency target, max-cost-per-request, and rollback policy.
   - Pilot with 3 paying customers.
2) 12-month:
   - Multi-tier fidelity graph (3+ variants), adaptive quantization profiles, and predictive switching based on device/geo.
   - Integrated billing primitives to credit customers for fidelity shifts and automated upgrade recommendations.

Success metrics:
- Reduce latency SLO miss rate for pilot customers by >= 40% without increasing per-token cost by more than 15% on average.
- Adoption: 20% of active routes in beta customers using LAFG within 6 months of GA.
- Developer satisfaction: NPS > 30 for route-level fidelity controls.

Product description / How it works:
1) Policy model: routes declare a latency objective (target p95 in ms), an allowance for tail latency, and a quality budget (relative score or absolute metric). Policies also accept a list of compatible model variants and a fallback priority.
2) Decision engine: at request arrival, the Gateway consults a compact decision graph that uses recent telemetry (latency, queue length, recent quality regression scores) and returns a fidelity decision. The decision contains: selected model variant, quantization profile, batching hint, and a truncation policy.
3) Execution: Redwood serving runtime enforces the selected fidelity with a short-lived execution config. KV cache and prefix caching are considered (can be reused only when compatibility rules pass).
4) Telemetry and audit: each decision is recorded with latency prediction, observed latency, quality probe outcomes (if available), and cost estimate.

Minimal API example (conceptual):

POST /v1/generate?route=my-chat-sso
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <key>
Body:
{
  "input": "Summarize the following document...",
  "lafg_policy": {
    "latency_target_ms": 150,
    "max_cost_per_1000_tokens_cents": 120,
    "quality_priority": "balanced",
    "variant_allowlist": ["rwd-7b-hf", "rwd-3b-fast"]
  }
}

(Implementation note: the field name and semantics will be part of the API stability discussion; this example is illustrative.)

Packaging and pricing implications:
- Basic (Hosted): LAFG available as a feature flag for hosted customers; no additional monthly fee, charged via per-token usage with optional fidelity-credits.
- Enterprise (Dedicated/Private): LAFG can be purchased as an SLA add-on that guarantees p95 routing latency targets with an SLO-backed commitment and a definable fallthrough credit pool.
- Credits model: customers can buy Fidelity Credits which are consumed when the decision engine upgrades to a higher-cost variant to meet quality objectives. Credits support escrows and rollback policies.

Recommended pricing tiers (draft):
| Tier | Feature | Billing unit | Notes |
| Basic | Policy UI + telemetry | Included | Per-token pricing applies |
| Fidelity Credits | Keeps access to higher variants | Per-credit | 1 credit approximates cost difference for 1000 tokens in typical conversational workload |
| SLA Add-on | Guaranteed p95 routing | Monthly subscription + credit pool | Minimum commit required for Dedicated |

Roadmap and phased rollout:
- Phase 0 (Design & Lab) - Q3 2026:
  - Validate decision-engine heuristics in lab with synthetic spike scenarios.
  - Define API contract and Console UX mockups.
- Phase 1 (Pilot) - Q4 2026:
  - Integrate with serving runtime for dynamic variant selection and short-lived config injection.
  - Navigate privacy review for telemetry in Private deployments.
- Phase 2 (GA Hosted) - Q1 2027:
  - General availability for Hosted tier with console controls, default policies, and basic fidelity credits.
- Phase 3 (Enterprise & Dedicated) - Q2 2027:
  - SLA-backed routing, credit escrows, and on-premise policy broker for Private customers.

Operational considerations and SLOs:
- Decision latency budget: the gateway decision must add <= 2ms median overhead to request path; we target < 5ms p95.
- Telemetry retention: fidelity decisions and probe outcomes retained 90 days for hosted, configurable for Enterprise.
- Rollback and safety: automatic fallback to default variant if decision engine internal error rate exceeds 0.1% or if quality probes detect >5% degradation on a rolling 1-hour window.

Telemetry and observability:
- Exposed metrics: decision_latency_ms, decision_outcome{variant}, fidelity_credit_consumed, policy_violations, per-route_p95_latency_post_decision.
- Console dashboards: per-route drift, credit consumption vs budget, quality probe heatmap, and cost delta analysis.

Security and compliance notes:
- No customer content is stored outside existing retention policies. Fidelity decisions may include hashed route identifiers for aggregated telemetry in Hosted.
- Private deployments require a local policy broker to avoid sending route-level telemetry off-prem unless customer opts in.

Open risks and mitigations:
1) Quality regressions from frequent switching: mitigate with sticky decisions when cache reuse probability is high and with canarying for new quantization profiles.
2) Billing complexity: mitigate with explicit UI that simulates expected credit consumption per route and a dry-run API.
3) Incompatibilities across variants: maintain a compatibility matrix and automatic downgrade paths; disallow cache reuse when compatibility unknown.

Ownership and next steps:
- Product lead: Maya Chen (owner)
- Engineering: runtime team (kernel-and-scheduling), platform (smart-routing), and console UX squad
- Short term actions (next 30 days):
  1) Finalize API field names and policy schema.
  2) Build lab runner to simulate real traffic topologies and fidelity switches.
  3) Draft initial Console wireframes and internal pricing proposal.

Appendix: sample policy schema (YAML sketch)

policy_id: chat-low-latency
latency_target_ms: 150
max_cost_per_1000_tokens_cents: 120
variants:
  - id: rwd-3b-fast
    priority: 1
  - id: rwd-7b-hf
    priority: 0
quality_priority: balanced
cache_reuse: conditional
